title: A 0.52% old-water limit permits zero A20 mean-age change in 2012-2021 at 2% tracer bounds and a 200-year age cap
abstract: We test how a small old-water fraction changes dual-tracer bounds on mean-age change. We rebuild six A20 and seven A22 paired bins on sigma0 26.5 from GLODAPv2.2023 in 2012 and 2021. Linear programs minimize a common upper limit q on the fraction older than 50 years in every bin and year. They impose full saturation, atmospheric CFC-12 and SF6 histories, 2% relative tracer bounds and zero section-mean age change. With a 200-year age cap, A20 needs q = 0.5114%; tracer fits alone need q = 0. A22 still requires at least 0.3067 years of mean-age rise at that cap, even with an unrestricted old fraction. At a 500-year cap, A22 permits zero mean change with q = 1.0827%. At 5% tracer bounds and a 200-year cap, the limits are 0% and 0.6956%. Zero change separately in every bin is a stronger condition and fails on both sections at 2% and a 200-year cap. The result quantifies the fragility of hard age cutoffs. It is not an estimate of old-water abundance or an oxygen attribution. Unknown saturation, partial-pressure mixing, sparse cruises and free age spectra limit physical use. Code, aggregate bounds, input hashes and external-scratch reproduction are included.

display.caption: Minimum old-water fraction limits and section-mean age-change bounds under the stated dual-tracer source model. Shading gives feasible sets, not confidence intervals.
